risk_note: RV2 by PR (identity port export and app wiring beside notification RV1). Builds the push send core: record(trx) writes the inbox message, the inbox log and the push log (queued, or suppressed / push_disabled when the recipient's category switch is off) in the caller's transaction and never calls the channel; dispatch(db) owns its transactions (refuses a transaction handle): it locks the push log, re-reads the category switch (off -> suppressed, no channel call), locks and re-checks the recipient's push_tokens rows per BR-ID-07 send-time checks (not revoked, not frozen at the injected Clock, bound sid's session not revoked and refresh strictly later than now, via a new identity read port) and conditionally unbinds failing rows by the (user_id, bound_sid) read at check time, records failed when no token is left, then commits the claim (row_version 0 -> 1) before calling the channel; a second transaction re-checks and calls the demo MobPush channel (no network, no forged vendor payloads, hard rule 7) and writes the result under a savepoint. An event key calls the channel at most once: retries resume only an unclaimed push, an attempted push whose result is unknown stays queued and is never resent. Payload is message_id, title and body only (BR-ID-10). Inbox is always written (BR-WATCH-15, BR-TEXT-09 example 5). Design converged over Codex review rounds r1-r5 under orchestrator rulings D10-170 and D10-172 (rule tests rewritten in the test phase to record, commit, then dispatch). No money, no attribution.
